slides.title: Code comes in / [units]
slides.text: A reader looks up a function, a method or a class. Each chunk holds one whole unit and its location:

steps: Parse the file into a syntax tree: Python's `ast`, or tree-sitter for most other languages.
Make one chunk per function or method, decorators included.
Put the file path, the class and the module constants it reads on top.
Split an oversized function between statements; each part repeats the signature.

slides.title: The method split / needs a [tab]
slides.text: LangChain's `from_language(Language.PYTHON)` tries these separators in order (langchain-text-splitters 1.1.3):
bullets:
`
	def ` matches a method indented with a tab. PEP 8 says "Use 4 spaces per indentation level", so methods fall through to `

Same file at 250 characters: chunk 4 of 6 starts at `if amount > LIMIT:`, the same cut as the character splitter.

slides.title: Decorators get / [left] behind
slides.text: When a chunk boundary falls on a `\ndef `, the `def` starts the new chunk and the decorator above it stays in the old one:

visuals.label: Chunk 5 of 6
Chunk 6 of 6

slides.after: Chunk 6 no longer says that `sync_refunds` retries. A route decorator such as `@app.get("/refunds")` gets stranded the same way.

slides.title: Tree-sitter keeps / the [decorator]
slides.text: LlamaIndex `CodeSplitter(language="python", max_chars=250)` packs whole syntax-tree nodes up to the limit:

visuals.label: Chunk 8 of 8

bullets: A node over the limit is split into its children, so `class RefundService:` and `def refund(self, order, amount):` each became a chunk of their own.
The body of `refund` came next, with no function name.

slides.title: Size it with / [max_chars]
slides.text: In llama-index-core 0.14.25, `CodeSplitter` sizes chunks by `max_chars` (default 1,500), or by `max_tokens` (default 512) with `count_mode="token"`.

visuals.code:
CodeSplitter(language="python")
# 778-character file -> {{1 chunk}}
CodeSplitter(language="python",
    chunk_lines=5, chunk_lines_overlap=2)
# -> the same 1 chunk

bullets: `chunk_lines` (default 40) and `chunk_lines_overlap` (15) are stored, but the split code doesn't read them, so chunks get no overlap.
Set `max_chars` for your embedding model, and check the behavior in the version you install.

slides.title: Give each chunk / its [address]
slides.text: A small chunker on Python's `ast` module: one chunk per function or method, with a header on top. Chunks 3 and 4 of 4 at 1,500 characters:
bullets: Start each chunk at the first decorator: `ast` keeps the `def` line in `lineno` and the decorators in `decorator_list`.
Constants the function reads join the header: `LIMIT = Decimal("500")` goes with `refund`.

slides.title: Split long ones, / keep the [signature]
slides.text: At 250 characters, `refund` splits between statements, and each part repeats the signature:

visuals.label: Part 2 of 3

bullets: Cut only between the body's top-level statements, so an `if` stays with its `raise`.
Each part's header lists only the constants that part reads: parts 1 and 3 leave `LIMIT` out.

slides.title: Search found / the [imports]
slides.text: BM25 keyword search (`rank_bm25`) over each splitter's chunks at 250 characters, a stand-in for functions longer than your chunk size. Query: "Where is the 500 refund limit checked?"

options.note: The check and the 500 in one chunk

slides.after: The 500 sits in a module constant; the header copies it into the chunk that runs the check.

cards.title: Use it when
items: Questions name a function, a class or a behavior inside one
The language has a parser: `ast` for Python, tree-sitter for most others
Most functions fit your chunk size

cards.title: Move on when
items: Answers follow calls across files: retrieve the callers and callees too
Files are generated or minified, with no useful function boundaries
The question is about a whole module: index a file summary as well

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: One chunk per function, decorators included
Header: file path, class, constants the code reads
LangChain's Python method separator is `\n\tdef `: tabs only
A `\ndef ` split can strand a decorator one chunk up
Long functions: every part repeats the signature
Test with a real question: which chunk comes back?

slides.line: A table has the same problem as a long function: split it by rows, and repeat the header row in every chunk.
